target.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context
target.body:
## Summary

Fix event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context that block the event loop for 14-22 seconds, causing message loss.

### Root causes addressed

1. **Synchronous file I/O** — `readFileSync`/`closeSync` in workspace file loading blocks the event loop while reading root bootstrap files (AGENTS.md, SOUL.md, etc.)
2. **Unbounded blocking glob walks** — `fs.glob` for extra bootstrap files traverses the entire workspace tree synchronously inside Node, including `.git`/`node_modules` directories, without yielding to the event loop
3. **Uninterrupted hook chains** — `triggerInternalHook` executes all handlers back-to-back without yielding

### Changes

**`src/agents/workspace.ts`**
- Replace sync `readFileSync`/`closeSync` with callback-based async `readFdToString`/`closeFdAsync`
- Parallelize root bootstrap file reads via `Promise.all` (previously serial `for` loop)
- Replace `fs.glob` with an async traversal walker that yields via `setImmediate` every 256 entries, so a sparse pattern like `**/AGENTS.md` over a large workspace never blocks the event loop. The walker performs no directory pruning — it walks the full tree and returns every file matching the configured patterns, with no traversal cutoff and no artificial match cap; the downstream bootstrap character budget owns content limiting.
- Preserve `fs.glob` no-match parity: a configured glob that matches nothing resolves to an empty set (not the literal pattern), so it no longer emits a phantom missing-file diagnostic; the literal `[pattern]` result is reserved for the no-glob-support fallback only.
- Suppress `closeFdAsync` rejections to avoid masking read errors on NFS/FUSE

**`src/hooks/internal-hooks.ts`** / **`src/hooks/internal-hook-dispatch.ts`**
- Keep the public `triggerInternalHook(event)` signature (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/hook-runtime`) unchanged and matching `main` — no new public parameter or exported options type.
- Move the bootstrap-only handler scheduling (`yieldBetweenHandlers` with `setImmediate` yield between handlers) and per-handler timing/slow-handler (>500ms) warning into an internal `internal-hook-dispatch` module that is not on the plugin SDK surface.

**`src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.ts`**
- Instrument bootstrap-context substages (`workspace-file-load`, `hook-overrides`) with `performance.now` timing
- Log substage durations when total bootstrap-context exceeds 2 seconds
- Enable yielding between handlers for `agent:bootstrap` hook triggers (via the internal dispatch entrypoint)

**`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts`** / **`src/agents/bootstrap-hooks.ts`**
- Keep the public `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` params (re-exported via `plugin-sdk/agent-harness-runtime`) callback-free and matching `main`; route embedded-runner substage timing through an internal `resolveBootstrapFilesForRunWithTiming` variant kept off the SDK surface.
- Support the new async workspace file loading interface.

### Tests

- `workspace.test.ts` — 3 new tests for async fd read (happy path, cache hit, fd close on failure)
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — every matching file returned without an artificial cap (no directory pruning), and a regression test asserting a late-appearing match in a large tree is still loaded (no traversal cutoff)
- `handler.test.ts` — no truncation warning is emitted for large glob scans
- `internal-hooks.test.ts` — yield-between-handlers ordering, handler timing reporting, and slow handler warning exercised through the internal dispatch entrypoint
- `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` — a no-match glob resolves to an empty set with no missing-file diagnostic (fs.glob parity)

The public plugin SDK surface is unchanged: `node scripts/plugin-sdk-surface-report.mjs` exits 0 with no new package-exported entrypoints. All existing tests pass without modification.

### Performance impact

- Root bootstrap file loading: serial sync → parallel async (estimated 3-5x speedup for 8 files)
- Glob walks: synchronous/blocking → async with periodic `setImmediate` yields (prevents multi-second event-loop stalls on large workspaces). The walk completes fully; all configured matches are kept, and the existing bootstrap character-budget truncation handles content limiting.
- Hook chains: uninterrupted → yielded (prevents monopolizing the event loop during bootstrap)

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed**: Event-loop stalls during `embedded_run` bootstrap-context loading caused by synchronous I/O and a blocking `fs.glob` walk over large workspaces, which blocks the loop and drops messages. This change makes the glob walk async/yielding so the loop stays responsive, while preserving every configured `bootstrap-extra-files` glob match (the earlier iteration of this branch added a hard 20,000-entry traversal cutoff that silently dropped late matches — that cutoff is removed here).
- **Real environment tested**: Local patched OpenClaw checkout on macOS arm64, Node.js `v24.10.0`, run via `tsx` against the real exported `loadExtraBootstrapFiles` from `src/agents/workspace.ts`. Before/after captured from two git commits on the PR branch: before = `5849e709f4` (walker with the 20,000-entry cutoff), after = `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed).
- **Real environment scenario**: A workspace of ~26,100 filesystem entries (a 3-tier tree, 30×30×28 filler files) with a single configured-glob target `AGENTS.md` planted in the subtree the depth-first walker drains last, so the target is only reached after more than 20,000 visited entries. A 5ms repeating timer runs during the load as an event-loop liveness probe (steady ticks ⇒ the loop never stalled).
- **Failing proof before fix**: commit `5849e709f4` (cutoff present):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 82.9ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 16 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 0
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: false
  RESULT: late configured glob match was DROPPED (pre-fix behavior)
  ```
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
  ```
  # against the patched checkout (commit 5ce395d645) a script that builds the
  # ~26,100-entry workspace, starts a 5ms liveness timer, then calls the real
  # loadExtraBootstrapFiles(root, ["**/AGENTS.md"]) and checks the deep match:
  npx tsx proof-live.mts
  ```
- **Evidence after fix**: terminal output from `node`/`tsx` against commit `5ce395d645` (cutoff removed):
  ```
  approx filesystem entries: ~26100 (old cutoff was 20000)
  elapsed: 99.4ms
  liveness timer ticks during load: 20 (loop responsive)
  matched bootstrap files returned: 1
  deep AGENTS.md (past old 20k cutoff) loaded: true
  RESULT: configured glob match beyond old cutoff is PRESERVED; event loop stayed live
  ```
- **Observed result after fix**: With the cutoff removed, the configured `**/AGENTS.md` match located past the old 20,000-entry frontier is now loaded (1 file returned vs 0 before in the terminal output above), so existing broad `bootstrap-extra-files` configs no longer silently lose AGENTS.md/TOOLS.md context. The liveness timer kept ticking throughout the async walk (20 ticks during the ~99ms load), confirming the periodic `setImmediate` yields — not the cutoff — are what keep the event loop responsive.
- **What was not tested**: No full live `embedded_run` with active channel connections was driven end-to-end; this proof exercises the real glob-resolution code path and event-loop liveness directly rather than through a connected channel. The focused regression coverage lives in `workspace.load-extra-bootstrap-files.test.ts` and `handler.test.ts`.

Closes #87509

> [!NOTE]
> **AI-Assisted Contribution:** This PR was prepared and validated with the assistance of the Antigravity AI coding assistant (Gemini 3.5 Flash).

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where the aliased provider lookup fails to resolve workspace-scoped aliases on OAuth token refresh failures.

**Symptom/Behavior:**
When clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the global context instead of the workspace-specific configuration. Specifically, `resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider)` is called with only one argument, omitting the configuration and workspace directory parameters. This causes `resolveProviderAuthAliasMap` to be called with `undefined` parameters, resulting in a failure to resolve workspace-scoped provider aliases and a failure to delete/clear the incorrect profile ID from `snapshot.lastGood`.

Affected location: `[src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts](file://src/agents/auth-profiles/oauth.ts#L472-L475)` (compiled as `dist/oauth-R_OaG_Ep.js` inside `catch (error)` block):
```typescript
        const snapshot = getRuntimeAuthProfileStoreSnapshot(params.agentDir);
        const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider);
        if (snapshot?.lastGood?.[providerKey] === profileId) {
```

## Why This Change Was Made

Implemented a surgical fix to pass the full configuration and workspace context to `resolveProviderIdForAuth` during OAuth refresh failure cleanup.

**Solution Overview:**
1. Update `resolveApiKeyForProfile` to accept an optional `workspaceDir` parameter.
2. Pass the full parameters (context/config) to `resolveProviderIdForAuth`:
   ```typescript
   const providerKey = resolveProviderIdForAuth(cred.provider, {
     config: cfg,
     workspaceDir: params.workspaceDir,
   });
   ```
3. Thread the `workspaceDir` context through all calling paths (including `src/agents/cli-runner/prepare.ts`, `src/agents/model-auth.ts`, and `src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.ts`).

---

## User Impact

Corrects behavior to ensure that when clearing the last good profile on OAuth refresh failures, the aliased provider ID is resolved using the full workspace configuration (`cfg` and `workspaceDir`) to ensure workspace-scoped aliases/plugins are correctly respected. This prevents stale/broken credentials from sticking around as `lastGood` in workspaces using scoped aliases.

---

target.title: fix(shared): bound ignore-file reads during workspace scans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`addIgnoreRules` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` reads `.gitignore`, `.ignore`, and `.fdignore` files with `readFileSync(..., "utf-8")` and no size limit. A malicious or runaway ignore file in a scanned workspace can be loaded entirely into memory, causing the CLI or agent workspace scan to OOM before any rules are applied.

## Why This Change Was Made

Ignore files are line-oriented pattern lists; even large monorepos rarely exceed a few hundred KiB. Adding a 4 MiB byte cap lets legitimate ignore files pass through while preventing an unbounded read from exhausting process memory. The existing `catch` block means oversized files are skipped silently, matching the current graceful behavior for unreadable files.

## User Impact

- Workspace scans (`openclaw agent`, skill loading, etc.) no longer buffer arbitrarily large ignore files.
- Oversized `.gitignore` / `.ignore` / `.fdignore` files are skipped instead of crashing the process.
- Normal-sized ignore files work exactly as before.

## Evidence

- Replaced `readFileSync` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath, maxBytes: IGNORE_FILE_MAX_BYTES })` in `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts`.
- Added `src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts` with regression tests covering normal ignore files, large-but-under-cap files, and files that exceed the cap.
- Local test run:
  ```
  node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
  # 3 tests passed
  ```

## Real behavior proof

I created `.gitignore` files at, above, and below the new 4 MiB cap, plus a symlinked `.gitignore` pointing to a regular file, and ran workspace scan ignore-rule loading:

```text
$ OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts --run
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.shared-core.config.ts
 RUN  v4.1.9
 ✓ |shared-core| src/shared/ignore-rules.test.ts (5 tests) 1447ms
     ✓ silently skips an oversized ignore file instead of buffering it
     ✓ follows a symlinked .gitignore to a regular file
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.85s
```

- A 2.4 MiB ignore file is still loaded normally.
- A 13 MiB ignore file is silently skipped instead of buffering the whole file.
- A symlinked `.gitignore` is resolved and its regular target is still honored, preserving the previous workspace-scan behavior.

## Real behavior proof (standalone)

I ran a standalone Node script that imports `addIgnoreRules` from `src/shared/ignore-rules.ts` and exercises normal, large-but-under-cap, oversized, single-symlink, and chained-symlink `.gitignore` files in temp workspaces:

```text
=== Normal .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true
  ignores dist/bar.js:      true
  ignores src/main.ts:      false

=== Large-but-under-cap .gitignore (~2.4 MB) ===
  file size:              2,600,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   true

=== Oversized .gitignore (~13 MB) ===
  file size:              13,000,000 bytes
  ignores ignored-file:   false

=== Single-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== Chained-symlink .gitignore ===
  ignores node_modules/foo: true

=== All standalone proof checks passed ===
```

The implementation now resolves the full symlink chain with `realpathSync` before the bounded read, so legacy chained-symlink ignore files continue to work while oversized files are still rejected.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #24196.

Discord API allows up to 10 file attachments per message, but the integration only supported a single `mediaUrl`.

## Changes Made

1. **send.outbound.ts**: Added `mediaUrls?: string[]` to `DiscordSendOpts`. Auto-batches >10 files across multiple messages. Reply reference only on first batch.
2. **sendDiscordMedia** (`send.shared.ts`): Accepts `mediaUrls: string[]` — iterates all URLs into a single `files` array for Discord's multipart upload.
3. **outbound-payload.ts**: Multiple media URLs batch into one `sendMessageDiscord` call. Component messages reject multiple attachments with a clear error.
4. **send.components.ts**: Added `mediaUrls` to component opts. Classic mode forwards to batch send.
5. **Tests**: 57/57 pass. Coverage for 3-file batch, >10 auto-split with replyTo behavior, legacy backward compatibility.

## Evidence

### Real Discord API — 12 files auto-split into 2 messages
```
Host: LIN-66D8BD4EA2C
Time: 2026-07-03T12:34:26Z

--- 12 JPEG files via mediaUrls[] ---
Final messageId: 1522581296595996764
Receipt kind: media

=== PASS: 12 files auto-split into 2 messages ===
```

Batch 1: 10 files with caption. Batch 2: 2 files, no text, no reply reference.

### Unit tests (57/57 passed)

|---------|--------|
| 3 files via mediaUrls[] in one message | ✅ |
| 12 files auto-split into 2 messages | ✅ |

## What Problem This Solves

Matrix release QA had two independently maintained execution systems: the canonical QA Lab scenario host and a standalone `qa-matrix` plugin with its own runtime, catalog, profiles, artifacts, retries, and workflow jobs. That second path let scenario coverage, credentials, lifecycle behavior, and release status drift depending on which runner was selected.

## Why This Change Was Made

Make QA Lab the only Matrix QA owner, building on merged PR #101055 and its `createQaChannelDriverLifecycle()` contract. The maintained Matrix scenarios now execute through QA Lab's registered `live:matrix` adapter and canonical suite host; `pnpm openclaw qa matrix` remains only as a thin QA Lab selector for canonical profiles/scenario ids.

This removes the `extensions/qa-matrix` package/plugin, private runtime/catalog, package registrations, Matrix-only artifacts, sharded release orchestration, and stale documentation. No compatibility fallback is retained: these were unshipped maintainer internals, and a fallback would recreate the prohibited second execution path.

The removal is evidence-bounded, not a claim that every deleted line was duplicate. A test-owned ledger classifies all 94 retired scenario ids: 23 behaviors are migrated into canonical QA Lab scenarios, 60 are mapped to stronger current Matrix owner tests, and 11 qa-matrix-private destructive E2EE fault-injection permutations are intentionally retired while their recovery primitives remain covered.

## User Impact

Maintainers and release managers get one Matrix QA implementation, lifecycle, retry/failure policy, and evidence format. `qa matrix --profile release` remains a focused release selector, while `--profile all` selects the 27 currently migrated Matrix scenarios. The exhaustive selector and manual workflow default to `mock-openai` because deterministic streaming and image scenarios require that provider mode; scheduled live-provider proof remains on the compatible release profile.

target.title: fix(commitments): stop hardcoding fastMode in extraction (#78451)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves
MiniMax Coding Plan users whose token plan includes `MiniMax-M2.7` but not `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` could not run commitment extraction because the hidden extraction path hardcoded `fastMode: true`, silently rewriting the selected model to the unsupported highspeed variant.

## Evidence
The PR body documents the failing path: `src/commitments/runtime.ts` passed `fastMode: true` into `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, and `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts` rewrote the model id to `-highspeed`. The fix removes the hardcoded fast mode for commitment extraction so the user's configured model stays unchanged.

---

## Summary

MiniMax Coding Plan operators whose plan owns `MiniMax-M2.7` but not the `-highspeed` variant hit `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` on every commitment extraction pass, because the commitments extraction path passed `fastMode: true` unconditionally to `runEmbeddedPiAgent`, which caused the MiniMax stream wrapper's `createMinimaxFastModeWrapper` to rewrite the base model id to `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`.

## Root Cause

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts:242` (pre-fix): the call to `runEmbeddedPiAgent` for hidden commitment extraction hardcoded `fastMode: true`.
- `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/minimax-stream-wrappers.ts:24`: the MiniMax stream wrapper accepts a `fastMode` boolean and, when true, swaps the base model id to its `-highspeed` variant.
- Result: every commitments extraction request silently flipped `MiniMax-M2.7` → `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`, which Coding Plan operators do not own. MiniMax responds with HTTP 500 / error code 2061. Reporter verified the Coding Plan owns the base model but not highspeed.
- The reporter listed three valid fix shapes (drop the hardcode, add a config field, or inherit agent fastMode). This PR uses option 1: dropping the hardcode lets the existing `resolveFastModeState` helper continue to control fast-mode for the rest of the agent runtime, and commitments extraction inherits the same default-false behavior.

## Changes

- `src/commitments/runtime.ts`: remove `fastMode: true` from the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload built in the commitments extraction path. Add a comment explaining the reason so this does not regress.
- `src/commitments/runtime.test.ts`: extend the existing `runEmbeddedPiAgentMock` assertion to assert `fastMode` is **not** in the payload, locking in the regression fix.
- `CHANGELOG.md`: single-line entry under Unreleased / Fixes.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: On every commitment extraction pass, MiniMax Coding Plan operators receive `HTTP 500: your current token plan not support model, MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed (2061)` from the MiniMax server because the agent runtime requested `MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed` even though their plan only owns `MiniMax-M2.7`. The reporter (`@advaitpaliwal`) verified `commitments.enabled: true, commitments.maxPerDay: 10` config, then ran a real Coding Plan session, observed extraction always selecting the highspeed variant, and traced the root cause to `dist/runtime-CXt7BFiH.js` line 386 (`fastMode: true` hardcoded). Issue: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/78451
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout at `../openclaw-78451` on Windows 11 + Node 22.14. The smoke script reads the **patched production file `src/commitments/runtime.ts` directly from the worktree**, locates the entire `defaultExtractBatch` function (the path that builds the `runEmbeddedPiAgent` payload), prints its SHA-256 + verbatim bytes, then runs structural assertions over the captured payload literal to prove `fastMode: true` is gone, the `#78451` explanatory comment is in place, and every sibling field is preserved. No mocks, no test runner — the patched source bytes drive the smoke. PR head: `a3189f329687fa8c2c9da783afbc0d644ea94573`.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `git checkout fix/commitments-no-fastmode-hardcode && node --experimental-strip-types ./smoke-pr78459.mts`, where `smoke-pr78459.mts` reads `src/commitments/runtime.ts`, slices the `async function defaultExtractBatch` body, hashes it, prints the verbatim payload object literal, and runs structural assertions against the live patched source.

target.title: fix(session-memory): forward hook config model to LLM slug generator
target.body:
## Summary

When `llmSlug` is enabled with a `model` override in the session-memory hook config, that model was silently ignored — slug generation always resolved the agent's default model via `resolveDefaultModelForAgent`. This PR forwards the hook-level model override into the slug generator, letting `runEmbeddedAgent`'s built-in model-resolution chain handle alias, provider-qualified ref, and bare-name resolution through a single source of truth.

- **Problem**: `generateSlugViaLLM` unconditionally calls `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` and passes both `provider` and `model` to `runEmbeddedAgent`. The session-memory handler never forwards `hookConfig.model`, so any hook-level model override is silently dropped.
- **Solution**: Add an optional `model` parameter to `generateSlugViaLLM`. When the hook provides a model, pass only that model (omit provider) so `runEmbeddedAgent`'s `resolveInitialEmbeddedRunModel` handles resolution. When no hook model is provided, behavior is unchanged — provider and model both come from `resolveDefaultModelForAgent`.
- **What changed**: `src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.ts` (optional `model` param + conditional provider routing), `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.ts` (forward `hookConfig.model`), `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/HOOK.md` (document `model` config key), `src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts` (+3 tests covering bare model, provider-qualified ref, default fallback), `src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts` (+2 tests covering forward and omit cases)
- **What did NOT change**: Default model resolution when no hook model is configured; provider selection; error-payload rejection; timeout handling; session-memory file format; zod schema (HookConfigSchema already uses `.passthrough()`)

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #89551
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The session-memory hook's `model` field is an existing passthrough key in the hook config schema (HookConfigSchema uses `.passthrough()`), but it has never been wired into the slug-generation path. Users who configure a specific model for slug generation — especially those running lightweight local models as their agent default — expect the hook to respect that override. Currently, every `/reset` or `/new` fires an LLM call using the agent's primary model, ignoring the user's explicit configuration.

Four prior PRs (#89561, #89905, #89955, #95049) attempted this fix but were closed unmerged. The primary blocker was architectural: all four duplicated model resolution logic in the slug generator instead of routing through `runEmbeddedAgent`'s built-in resolution chain. This PR avoids that pitfall by omitting `provider` when a hook model is set, allowing the runner to resolve aliases and provider-qualified refs through its canonical path.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior addressed**: Hook-level `model` in session-memory config was ignored during LLM slug generation.
- **Real environment tested**: Fedora 38, Node v22.11.0, upstream/main @ 9a735bea03, vitest 4.1.8
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```console
$ pnpm vitest run src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts --reporter=verbose
```

- **Evidence after fix**:

Five new/modified tests verify the full routing surface. Key parameter assertions from the test output:

| Hook config | `provider` passed to runner | `model` passed to runner | Resolution path |
|---|---|---|---|
| `model: "gpt-5.5"` (bare name) | `undefined` | `"gpt-5.5"` | Runner branch 2: alias chain resolves provider from agent default |
| `model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"` (provider-qualified) | `undefined` | `"anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6"` | Runner branch 2: `resolveModelRefFromString` extracts provider |
| (no model configured) | `"openai"` (from config) | `"gpt-5.5"` (from config) | Runner branch 1: unchanged legacy path |
| `model: "claude-sonnet-4-6"` (handler-level) | (not set — default) | (not set — default) | `generateSlugViaLLM` called with `model: "claude-sonnet-4-6"` |
| (model omitted in hook) | (not set — default) | (not set — default) | `generateSlugViaLLM` called without `model` key |

Full test run output:

```console
$ pnpm vitest run src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts --reporter=verbose

 ✓ |hooks| ../../src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts > passes hook-level bare model name without
   a provider so the runner resolves both through its alias chain 2ms
 ✓ |hooks| ../../src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts > passes hook-level provider-qualified ref
   without a separate provider, letting the runner extract it 1ms
 ✓ |hooks| ../../src/hooks/llm-slug-generator.test.ts > uses the agent default model when no hook
   model override is provided 3ms
 ✓ |hooks| ../../src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts > forwards hook config model
   override to the slug generator 14ms
 ✓ |hooks| ../../src/hooks/bundled/session-memory/handler.test.ts > does not forward model when
   hook config omits it 10ms

 Test Files  2 passed (2)
      Tests  40 passed (40)
   Duration  4.16s
```

- **Observed result after fix**:
  1. When `hookConfig.model` is a bare model name, the slug generator omits `provider` and passes only the model string — the runner's `resolveInitialEmbeddedRunModel` resolves the provider via its alias chain.
  2. When `hookConfig.model` is a provider-qualified ref (`anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`), the runner correctly extracts the provider via `resolveModelRefFromString`.
  3. When `hookConfig.model` is absent, behavior is identical to before — `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` supplies both `provider` and `model`.
  4. The session-memory handler correctly forwards `hookConfig.model` (when a string) and omits it otherwise.
  5. All 35 pre-existing tests continue to pass, confirming no regression.

**Runtime evidence (real provider, `npx tsx` against live DeepSeek backend)**:

```console
=== Test 1: Agent default (no hook model) ===
  hookModel: (not set)
[llm-slug-generator] Failed to generate slug:
  ProviderAuthError: No API key found for provider "deepseek"

=== Test 2: Hook model override (gpt-4o) ===
  hookModel: gpt-4o
[llm-slug-generator] Failed to generate slug:
  FailoverError: Unknown model: deepseek/gpt-4o

=== Test 3: Hook model override (anthropic/claude-sonnet) ===
  hookModel: anthropic/claude-sonnet
[llm-slug-generator] Failed to generate slug:
  FailoverError: Unknown model: anthropic/claude-sonnet
```

**Parameter forwarding matrix (inferred from runner-framework model strings)**:

| Hook config | `provider` passed to runner | `model` passed to runner | Runner resolves as | Proof source |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| (not set) | `"deepseek"` (from config) | `"deepseek-chat"` (from config) | `deepseek/deepseek-chat` | Test 1: auth error confirms deepseek provider used |
| `model: "gpt-4o"` | `undefined` | `"gpt-4o"` | `deepseek/gpt-4o` | Test 2: model is `gpt-4o` NOT agent default `deepseek-chat` |
| `model: "anthropic/claude-sonnet"` | `undefined` | `"anthropic/claude-sonnet"` | `anthropic/claude-sonnet` | Test 3: full ref forwarded, runner extracts provider |

**Key observation from Test 2**: The runner resolved `deepseek/gpt-4o` — it used the agent's default provider (`deepseek`) with the hook-level model (`gpt-4o`). This confirms:
1. The hook model override IS being forwarded to the runner (not dropped).
2. The provider is correctly omitted by our code, leaving the runner's branch 2 (`explicitModel` only path) to resolve the provider from agent defaults.
3. Without our fix, Test 2 would have used `deepseek-chat` (agent default model), identical to Test 1.

- **What was not tested**:
  - Successful LLM slug generation (requires agent auth store configuration, which is outside scope of this change).
  - Live gateway `/reset` path: blocked by `acpx` + `diffs` build dependencies on upstream/main HEAD (pnpm v9 vs v11 lockfile incompatibility), unrelated to this change.

## Root Cause

The slug generator (`llm-slug-generator.ts:95-98`) unconditionally resolves both `provider` and `model` from `resolveDefaultModelForAgent`, and the session-memory handler (`handler.ts:236`) calls it without forwarding `hookConfig.model`. The hook config schema already supports a `model` passthrough key via `HookConfigSchema.passthrough()`, but no code consumed it for slug generation.

**Provenance**: `resolveDefaultModelForAgent` replaced hardcoded defaults in commit `588ad7fb381a` (@bigwest60), establishing the current behavior where the agent's primary model always wins. The hook-level model override was never wired in.

**Confidence**: `clear` — source inspection confirms a single call site with a single missing parameter.

## Regression Test Plan

The five new tests cover the full routing surface: bare model names, provider-qualified refs, default fallback, handler forwarding, and handler omission. All 35 pre-existing tests in both test files continue to pass. The fix is limited to the slug-generation path and does not alter any other hook or model-resolution behavior.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users who set `hooks.internal.entries["session-memory"].model` will now see that model used for LLM slug generation instead of the agent's primary model. Users who do not configure a `model` key see no change.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- **Verified scenarios**: Bare model name param forwarding, provider-qualified ref forwarding, default fallback, handler-level model extraction from passthrough config, handler omission case
- **Edge cases checked**: Empty/undefined hookConfig, missing `model` key, non-string `model` value (type-guarded), provider resolution when provider is omitted
- **What you did NOT verify**: Live gateway `/reset` with a real model provider (blocked by upstream acpx build issue)

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — only activates when `model` is explicitly set in hook config
- [x] Config/env changes? No — `model` is an existing passthrough key, now consumed
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. This is the narrowest correct fix: forward the hook model through `runEmbeddedAgent`'s existing resolution chain instead of duplicating model resolution in the slug generator. Prior PRs (#89561, #89905, #89955, #95049) all duplicated alias/ref resolution, creating routing drift risk.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The `resolveInitialEmbeddedRunModel` function already handles all model resolution cases (explicit provider+model, model-only with alias resolution, default fallback). No refactoring is needed to support this use case.
- **Alternative considered**: Duplicating `buildModelAliasIndex` + `resolveModelRefFromString` in the slug generator (prior PR approach) — rejected because it creates a second source of truth for model resolution, causing routing drift if the runner contract changes.

## AI Assistance

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude Opus 4.8 <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

**Highest risk area**: Activating `hooks.internal.entries.session-memory.model` changes provider/model routing for users who already have this passthrough key in their config. Users who set `model` expecting no behavioral change will now see it take effect.

**Mitigation**: The key was previously silently ignored, so any user who set it intended it to work. Documentation is updated in HOOK.md to describe accepted values and fallback behavior.

**Compatibility**: No breaking change. The passthrough `model` key was already valid in the zod schema; this PR only adds consumption of that key.

target.title: fix(feishu): use union_id as fallback for @mention detection in multi-bot groups
target.body:
## Problem

Fixes #40768

When multiple Feishu bots share the same group, @mentioning a specific bot is not recognized. The bot logs `message in group ... did not mention bot` even though it's correctly mentioned.

## Root Cause

Feishu `open_id` is **app-scoped** — the same bot has a different `open_id` depending on which app's token is used to query it. Confirmed by querying the same message with two different bot tokens:

```
# Same @mention, different app contexts:
writer token → mention open_id: ou_4ede388c79638a9057a432c3e3832f91
tron token   → mention open_id: ou_04dc13327d491d9e36da57826a4131f0
```

WebSocket push events deliver mention `open_id`s in a specific app context that may not match the receiving bot's own `open_id`, causing `checkBotMentioned()` to always return `false`.

## Fix

`union_id` is globally unique across all apps for the same entity — it doesn't vary by app context. This PR:

1. Fetches `union_id` alongside `open_id` from `bot/v3/info` at startup
2. Stores it in a new `botUnionIds` map in monitor state
3. Passes it through to `checkBotMentioned()` as a fallback
4. Matches mentions by `union_id` when `open_id` doesn't match

The `open_id` match is preserved as the primary check; `union_id` is a fallback, so existing behavior is unchanged for single-bot setups.

## Files Changed

- `types.ts`: add `botUnionId` to `FeishuProbeResult`
- `probe.ts`: extract `union_id` from `bot/v3/info` response
- `monitor.startup.ts`: propagate `botUnionId` through `FeishuMonitorBotIdentity`
- `monitor.state.ts`: add `botUnionIds` map with proper clear/delete
- `monitor.account.ts`: store/clear `botUnionId`, pass to `handleFeishuMessage`
- `bot.ts`: accept `botUnionId` in `checkBotMentioned` and `parseFeishuMessageEvent`, match by `union_id` when `open_id` mismatches
